mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost of capital, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over the same month signals a shift from speculative to fundamental demand in housing, reducing leverage-driven market volatility and resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month within the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over two consecutive months indicates a rise in labor force participation without a corresponding rise in unemployment, suggesting improved employment quality and productivity, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 3% signals an unexpected inflation shock not yet met with restrictive policy, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in GDPC1 for three consecutive quarters signals a deepening economic contraction, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.8%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.
